validity.recommendation: Treat 34 km / 12 in as unverified (GEM-only); demote refs to low/inferred and document that no independent source confirms the dimensions. Consider re-checking commodity classification (likely an associated-gas gathering/feeder line, not a dry-gas transmission trunk).
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: Ain Dar and Shedgum are both confirmed adjacent subfields of the Ghawar oil-and-gas field (independently corroborated: Saudipedia, NS Energy, CSEG/GeoExpro), roughly consistent with a ~34 km separation. Shedgum has hosted a gas plant processing associated gas since March 1980 (Fluor; Aramco/Saudipedia: ~450 MMcf/d of associated gas, sour-gas treating). A gas pipeline carrying associated gas from Ain Dar GOSPs to the Shedgum gas plant is therefore physically plausible and probably real as a piece of infrastructure. CAVEAT: I could find NO independent source that names a discrete 'Aindar-Shedgum gas pipeline' or that states its length (34 km) or diameter (12 in). Every search result affirming '34 km / 12 inch / operating / Saudi Aramco' traces back to the GEM wiki page itself (gem.wiki/Aindar-Shedgum_gas_pipeline) and cannot be used per standing rules. The GEM page's only listed citation is OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012 p.75 — a macro statistics table that would not contain a single field-pipeline's dimensions, so it does not support these specs. CLASSIFICATION: Independent Ain Dar<->Shedgum pipeline records that DO exist are for WATER injection, not gas — e.g. the Tekfen-built 56-in/80-km Qurrayah seawater-treatment-to-Ain Dar water-injection line (MEED) and the 'Ain Dar/Shedgum Sea Water Conversion Quad-1 Pipeline' (DMS Projects). FuelSource='Aindar' (an OIL field) plus a small 12-in bore and a destination of the Shedgum GAS PLANT all point to an associated-gas GATHERING/FEEDER line, not a Master Gas System dry-gas transmission trunk; this should be reviewed against how GEM classifies it (PipelineType/transmission vs gathering). SPEC: length and diameter are unconfirmed by any independent source and disagree with nothing only because nothing independent states them; per rules I treat them as GEM-only and do NOT silently pass them. DUPLICATE: compared against all 65 Saudi gas roster rows — no other ProjectID shares the Ain Dar->Shedgum endpoints or the 34 km/12 in spec; not a duplicate. ATTRIBUTION: owner/operator = Saudi Aramco is safe (all Ghawar/Shedgum gas infrastructure is Aramco-operated; corroborated by Fluor and Aramco corporate pages). Province: start should be Eastern Province (Ash Sharqiyah and Eastern Province are the same region — the StartState/Province='Ash Sharqiyah' vs EndState/Province='Eastern Province' inconsistency is cosmetic, same province). No verifiable URL states the pipeline's dimensions, so I am not fabricating a value-confirming ref; the attached refs are CONTEXTUAL support for the Shedgum-gas-plant/associated-gas classification reasoning only.

fills.researcher_notes: Owner/operator = Saudi Aramco. All Ghawar/Shedgum gas-gathering and processing infrastructure is Aramco-built and Aramco-operated; Fluor's own project record for the Shedgum Gas Plant names Saudi Aramco as client/operator. This confirms ownership of the system the pipeline feeds, not the discrete pipe's dimensions. Low tier because it is contextual (ownership of the connected facility), single-source for the specific pipe.

Fuel = Gas is consistent with the destination being the Shedgum gas plant, which processes associated gas (Saudipedia/Fluor). CAVEAT: this is associated/sour gas gathered from the Ain Dar GOSP area, so 'gas' is correct at the commodity level but the line is more likely a gathering/feeder line than a dry-gas transmission trunk — see the classification concern. Low tier: confirms the facility carries gas, not the specific pipe's spec.

summary: Aindar-Shedgum (P1924): real as Ghawar associated-gas infrastructure but 34 km/12 in specs are GEM-only (no independent confirmation) and the line looks like an associated-gas gathering/feeder to the Shedgum gas plant, not a dry-gas transmission trunk; spec+classification concern, not a duplicate.
